{{short description|All submatrices of a discrete Fourier transform matrix of prime length are invertible}}
{{Distinguish|Chebotarev's density theorem}}

The '''Chebotarev theorem on roots of unity''' was originally a conjecture made by [[Alexander Ostrowski|Ostrowski]] in the context of [[Lacunary function|lacunary series]].

[[Nikolai Chebotaryov|Chebotarev]] was the first to prove it, in the 1930s. This proof involves tools from [[Galois extension|Galois theory]] and pleased [[Alexander Ostrowski|Ostrowski]], who made comments arguing that it "''does meet the requirements of mathematical esthetics''".<ref>Stevenhagen et al., 1996</ref>
Several proofs have been proposed since,<ref>P.E. Frenkel, 2003</ref> and it has even been discovered independently by [[Jean Dieudonné|Dieudonné]].<ref>J. Dieudonné, 1970</ref>

== Statement ==

Let <math>\Omega </math> be a matrix with entries <math> a_{ij} =\omega^{ij},1\leq i,j\leq n </math>, where <math>\omega =e^{2\mathrm i\pi / n},n\in \mathbb{N}</math>. 
If <math>n</math> is prime then any minor of <math> \Omega </math> is non-zero.

Equivalently, all [[Submatrix|submatrices]] of a [[DFT matrix]] of prime length are invertible.

== Applications ==
In [[signal processing]],<ref>Candès, Romberg, Tao, 2006</ref> the theorem was used by [[Terence Tao|T. Tao]] to extend the [[Uncertainty principle#Signal processing|uncertainty principle]].<ref>T. Tao, 2003</ref>
